newsitem.title: THAILAND: Asian central banks vow to stabilise currencies.
newsitem.headline: Asian central banks vow to stabilise currencies.

text.p: Top officials from nine Asian central banks agreed at a meeting here on Saturday to strengthen cooperation to maintain the stability of regional currencies, a Thai central bank official told Reuters on Sunday.

"After exchanging views on the recent volatility in the foreign exchange markets, we jointly agreed to strengthen our cooperation to maintain the stability of currencies in the region," said a Bank of Thailand senior official.
The Bank of Thailand in a separate statement said the top Asian monetary officials gathered here as part of the regular meeting of Executives' Meeting of East Asia and Pacific (EMEAP) Central Banks.

The meeting, which was held without publicity, included senior central bankers and top monetary officials from Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, South Korea, Indonesia, China, Hong Kong and Thailand, the official said.
The baht came under speculative attack 10 day ago, and the Thai central bank, the Monetary Authority of Singapore and other regional monetary authorities jointly intervened to defend the currency.
The selling pressure on the baht spilled over to other regional currencies and financial markets as investors were jittery about the outlook for the region as a whole.
The BOT has also been squeezing short-term liquidity for offshore speculators by ordering onshore banks not to lend short-term baht to them.
The baht recovered significantly since the central bank launched the measure.

Offshore dealers had been said to incur substantial loss from the central bank's move by being forced to pay extremely high interest rates for baht borrowing to cover their short positions, analysts said.
The central bank's measure had remained effective until last Friday and is likely to continue next week, dealers said.
